finding.claim: Unknown kid in an unverified JWT header forces an unthrottled synchronous JWKS HTTP fetch on every request (low severity, availability / outbound amplification). Precondition: the application calls get_signing_key_from_jwt on unauthenticated input.
finding.source: jwks_client.py:224-226 - header.get('kid') read from unverified token header before any signature check
finding.sink: jwks_client.py:203 get_signing_keys(refresh=True) -> :153 fetch_data -> :118 urllib.request.urlopen (30 s timeout)

trace.note: decode_token with verify_signature=False reads unverified header
cached lookup via get_signing_keys() misses for unknown kid

finding.guards_checked: kid type check at api_jws.py:430-432 (type only, not bounded or rate-limited); no negative caching (lru_cache at jwks_client.py:100-104 does not cache exceptions); no rate limit anywhere in the call path; no enforced control prevents repeated refetch per attacker request.

finding.claim: JSON header parsing catches only ValueError, so deeply nested JSON in an unauthenticated token raises RecursionError that escapes the PyJWT error hierarchy (low severity; error-handling / availability). Same root cause also applies to signed-claim validators that catch only ValueError (api_jwt.py:477-481, 492-494, 506-510), where a validly signed token with a null or infinite iat/nbf/exp raises TypeError or OverflowError. Not verified by execution; based on CPython json semantics.
finding.source: api_jws.py:318-321 - attacker-supplied token string (E1) and header JSON segment
finding.sink: api_jws.py:337 json.loads(header_data) inside try/except ValueError at :338; claim validators api_jwt.py:477, 492, 506

trace.note: except ValueError does not catch RecursionError
int(payload['iat']) except ValueError only; signed-token variant

finding.guards_checked: ValueError handling at api_jws.py:338 and api_jwt.py:298-300 (payload JSON); claim validators catch only ValueError; no catch-all converts these to PyJWTError. Signature check happens after header parsing, so the header path is reachable pre-authentication. Claim-validator path needs a validly signed token or verify_signature=False with explicit verify_* options.

finding.claim: Issuer validation fails open when the application omits the issuer argument: _validate_iss returns early on issuer None while verify_iss defaults to True, unlike _validate_aud which fails closed. Conditional: exploitable only if the app omits issuer= and shares key material across multiple issuers or tenants. Documented opt-in API behaviour; reported as a design weakness.
finding.source: Token signed by a key the application trusts, issued by a different issuer or tenant (attacker must hold such a token)
finding.sink: api_jwt.py:412-413 _validate_iss call returns early at :568 when issuer is None, so token is accepted

trace.note: if issuer is None: return (no check)
contrast: _validate_aud raises InvalidAudienceError when audience None and aud claim present

finding.guards_checked: verify_iss option (default True) gives the appearance of enforcement but the check is skipped when issuer is None. Signature verification still applies, so the attacker must hold a validly signed token from a trusted key. _validate_sub at api_jwt.py:452 has the same fail-open pattern and was not reported separately.
